title: Arrest and recovery of function in symptomatic Alzheimer’s disease

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a disease-modifying treatment that durably stops clinical decline and restores meaningful cognitive ability and everyday function after Alzheimer’s symptoms begin. Recovery would mean regaining abilities that matter in daily life, potentially including greater independence. The initial proposed demonstration concerns people with mild cognitive impairment or mild dementia due to Alzheimer’s disease. Whether the same capability could extend to advanced disease remains a separate question. This is the target capability defined by the supplied research and review.

The supplied lecanemab evidence illustrates the clinical gap. In an 18-month randomized trial, amyloid burden decreased and average clinical worsening slowed, while average impairment still increased. Amyloid reduction, slower decline, sustained stabilization, and recovery therefore require distinct clinical demonstrations. The proposed innovation would need to establish both durable arrest and meaningful recovery.

significance.text: As a conditional impact assessment, durable arrest plus recovery could fundamentally change the trajectory of symptomatic Alzheimer’s disease. Preserving cognition and restoring daily abilities could allow affected people to retain or regain independence and could reduce the assistance families and professional caregivers must provide. The size of those benefits would depend on the degree of recovery, its duration, the disease stages treated, and treatment safety and accessibility.

The supplied clinical comparison establishes why the target would represent a substantial advance over the particular result documented here. Lecanemab produced less average worsening over 18 months, with continued average deterioration in both trial groups. These findings do not establish a fixed number of months gained or a return of lost independence.

Broader consequences are conditional possibilities. Durable functional recovery could change long-term care needs and the economics of aging societies, but the supplied evidence does not quantify those effects. Success in early symptomatic Alzheimer’s disease would establish benefits within the population studied. Advanced Alzheimer’s disease, Parkinson’s disease, frontotemporal dementia, and vascular brain injury would each require their own evidence. Preventing or delaying symptoms in an asymptomatic population is also a separate clinical outcome from restoring function after impairment.

missing_breakthrough.text: The unresolved capability within the supplied evidence is the combination of sustained clinical stabilization and restoration of lost function after symptoms appear. The lecanemab abstract demonstrates amyloid reduction accompanied by slower average deterioration, leaving that combined capability unestablished by this trial. It does not determine whether an arrest-and-recovery intervention became available elsewhere or at a later date.

The research identifies tau pathology, synapse and neuron loss, inflammation, and circuit dysfunction as candidate downstream or parallel barriers. These retain explanatory value as proposed biological obstacles. The supplied abstract, however, does not establish their respective causal contributions, identify which must be treated to achieve recovery, or show which impairments remain reversible. A successful approach would need to determine how much functional restoration can come from rescuing surviving neural systems and whether additional repair or replacement is necessary.

As an engineering synthesis, the challenge includes connecting biological changes to durable improvements in cognition and daily activities, identifying patients with recoverable capacity, and delivering treatment with an acceptable burden of adverse effects and monitoring. If multiple disease processes require intervention, their treatment sequence and combined safety would also need investigation. The supplied material does not establish a particular drug, combination, regenerative method, or delivery platform as sufficient.

current_state.text: The supplied evidence centers on Clarity AD, reported online in November 2022 and published in the January 5, 2023 issue of the New England Journal of Medicine. This phase 3 randomized trial enrolled 1,795 participants with early Alzheimer’s disease, including mild cognitive impairment or mild dementia, and followed them for 18 months. It provides a dated demonstration of amyloid reduction accompanied by slower clinical decline.

Adjusted mean worsening on the Clinical Dementia Rating–Sum of Boxes, or CDR-SB, was 1.21 points with lecanemab and 1.66 points with placebo at 18 months. The between-group difference was −0.45 points. The authors characterized the clinical effect as a moderate reduction in decline across cognition and function. Both groups worsened on average. Group averages alone do not establish whether particular participants improved, and the supplied abstract does not demonstrate durable clinical arrest or restoration of lost function.

Amyloid-related imaging abnormalities involving edema or effusions occurred in 12.6% of participants receiving lecanemab. This finding makes treatment safety a substantive part of the proposed breakthrough. The abstract also identifies longer trials as necessary to determine longer-term efficacy and safety. The supplied review does not provide a hemorrhage rate or enough detail to establish safety across broader clinical populations.

The source reviewed was the verified PubMed abstract record. The review did not inspect the full article, figures, or a donanemab report. The research also states that donanemab reduces plaque and slows decline, but that assertion remains unverified within the supplied evidence and no donanemab effect sizes can be established here. This limitation leaves the claim open for source verification.

The source index records retrieval on November 1, 2026, with no extraction issues reported for the saved record. That retrieval date does not update the trial’s clinical findings or establish the treatment landscape in 2026. The supplied freshness record is empty, so the evidence supports the dated Clarity AD results while leaving subsequent developments and comparative treatment rankings unresolved.

completion_criteria.text: A proposed convincing demonstration would be a randomized controlled trial in people with mild cognitive impairment or mild dementia due to Alzheimer’s disease, followed for several years. It would show sustained stabilization on prespecified measures of cognition and daily function, together with a substantial fraction of treated participants regaining clinically meaningful abilities from baseline. Favorable between-group comparisons would be required alongside absolute trajectories, so that a claim of arrest and recovery can be evaluated directly. The duration and recovery thresholds proposed here require justification in a trial protocol.
completion_criteria.label: Randomized trial demonstrates sustained stabilization and clinically meaningful recovery

completion_criteria.text: The protocol should define numerical thresholds for meaningful improvement, the proportion of participants expected to improve, and the daily abilities that would count as regained independence. Repeated assessments and prespecified analyses should distinguish durable gains from measurement variability, practice effects, and temporary symptomatic changes. Amyloid clearance or another biomarker change could support a biological explanation, while clinical outcomes would establish whether people actually regained function.
completion_criteria.label: Prespecified clinical thresholds distinguish durable recovery from transient improvement

completion_criteria.text: Safety criteria should prespecify acceptable frequencies and severity of edema, hemorrhage, and other serious adverse events, together with treatment discontinuation and monitoring requirements. The 12.6% edema or effusion finding in the supplied lecanemab trial grounds the need to assess such harms. It does not define an acceptable threshold for a future treatment. Practical acceptability would depend on the magnitude and durability of benefit, patient risk, and the care setting.
completion_criteria.label: Prespecified safety criteria define acceptable harms and monitoring requirements

completion_criteria.text: A proposed reproducibility requirement is confirmation in independent studies and across multiple clinical centers, with transparent reporting of individual response distributions, attrition, adverse events, and relevant patient subgroups. Follow-up should establish how long benefit persists and whether continuing treatment is necessary. Demonstrations should specify disease stage, eligibility restrictions, delivery requirements, and feasible monitoring. Successful finite trials would establish the breadth demonstrated in those populations, with additional evidence needed for advanced disease or wider clinical use.
completion_criteria.label: Independent studies confirm durable benefits across multiple clinical centers

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis links CLM-03 most closely to CLM-04, Restoration of adult human central nervous system circuitry after injury. Both concern recovery of meaningful neurological function and may involve synaptic or circuit repair. CLM-03 additionally requires control of the Alzheimer’s disease process while function recovers. CLM-04 addresses circuitry restoration after injury, and success in either entry would leave the other’s disease-specific requirements to be demonstrated.

CLM-08, Safe multi-tissue reversal of human biological aging, overlaps through the possibility that restoring tissue resilience could benefit brain function. Its target spans multiple tissues and biological aging. CLM-03 requires direct evidence of arrest and functional recovery in symptomatic Alzheimer’s disease, regardless of whether an intervention changes aging measures. Either achievement would require separate evidence to establish the other.

CLM-09, Curative in vivo genome writing beyond the liver, could provide an enabling platform if a future Alzheimer’s intervention required genetic changes in relevant cells. CLM-01, Programmable antigen-specific immune tolerance, offers a narrower potential connection if a disease-relevant immune mechanism suitable for antigen-specific tolerance were established. These are hypothetical mechanistic links based on the roster. The supplied evidence identifies neither platform as necessary or sufficient for CLM-03.

CLM-06, Therapeutic remuscularization of the adult human heart, and CLM-15, Restoration of nephron number in the adult human kidney, share the broad goal of recovering organ capacity after damage. Their specified endpoints concern cardiac muscle and nephron restoration. CLM-03 is defined by clinical arrest and recovered cognitive and daily function, leaving the biological route to that recovery open.

unresolved_issues: The supplied evidence does not establish whether any intervention achieved durable arrest and recovery after the dated Clarity AD report or by November 1, 2026.
The causal importance, treatment requirements, and reversibility of the proposed tau, inflammatory, synaptic, neuronal, and circuit barriers remain unresolved within the supplied material.
The donanemab assertion requires an appropriate primary source before its findings, population, effect sizes, or safety can be integrated as established results.
Individual improvement patterns, long-term trajectories, and detailed safety outcomes cannot be determined from the reviewed abstract alone.
Numerical definitions of sustained stabilization, meaningful recovery, a substantial responder fraction, acceptable harm, and adequate follow-up remain to be specified and justified.
Applicability to advanced Alzheimer’s disease, broader patient populations, and routine clinical delivery remains unestablished.

The review’s recommendation to remove the donanemab assertion was adopted as removal from established findings. Its existence in the research was retained as an explicitly unverified claim to preserve uncertainty.

brief.title: Stopping Alzheimer’s decline and regaining daily abilities
possible: People whose Alzheimer’s symptoms have begun could regain lost thinking skills and everyday abilities, while treatment keeps further decline from returning. The first goal is recovery in people with mild memory and thinking impairment or mild dementia.
why: Regaining daily abilities could help people recover independence. Lasting recovery could also reduce the assistance families and professional caregivers need to provide, changing long-term care needs.

sources.who: Christopher H van Dyck and collaborators
sources.showed: In a randomized trial, lecanemab reduced amyloid, a protein that builds up in the brain, and slowed worsening of thinking and daily function. Both groups still worsened on average.
sources.quote: Lecanemab reduced markers of amyloid in early Alzheimer's disease and resulted in moderately less decline on measures of cognition and function than placebo at 18 months but was associated with adverse events.
sources.cited_for: Reducing amyloid can slow clinical decline in early Alzheimer’s disease.
sources.not_established: The trial did not demonstrate lasting stabilization together with recovery of lost abilities.

sources.who: Jennifer A Zimmer and colleagues at Eli Lilly and Company
sources.showed: Donanemab slowed progression over 3 years compared with a separate observational group. Slower progression also persisted among participants who completed treatment early.
sources.quote: Clinical benefits of donanemab continued after the treatment course was completed.
sources.cited_for: Slower decline may persist after a limited course of treatment.
sources.not_established: The extension used an external comparison group and did not establish lasting arrest plus recovery.

sources.who: Christopher H van Dyck and collaborators
sources.showed: Lecanemab’s follow-up study reported continued benefits in thinking, function and quality of life. Participants with less amyloid or tau, another disease-related protein, showed stability or improvement.
sources.quote: Across clinical and HRQoL endpoints, lecanemab‐treated participants continued to benefit through 36 months.
sources.cited_for: Some participants with less disease-related protein buildup showed stability or improvement during longer treatment.
sources.not_established: Participants knew they received treatment; subgroup findings do not establish lasting recovery in a randomized comparison.

shown: Lecanemab and donanemab have slowed decline in early Alzheimer’s disease. Longer follow-up has found continued benefit, including stability or improvement in a lecanemab subgroup. These findings bring recovery into focus, but do not yet demonstrate lasting arrest and meaningful recovery together.
missing: A randomized trial has yet to demonstrate lasting stabilization together with meaningful recovery of thinking and daily abilities.
Recovery thresholds must distinguish regained abilities from test variability, practice and temporary symptom relief.
Acceptable harms and monitoring demands must be established alongside durable benefits.
Independent studies must confirm who benefits, how long recovery lasts and whether treatment must continue.

milestones.label: A randomized trial demonstrates lasting stabilization and recovery
milestones.explanation: A randomized trial in early symptomatic Alzheimer’s would have to show lasting stabilization and meaningful regained abilities over several years. This would establish both parts of the goal.

milestones.label: Defined thresholds distinguish durable recovery from temporary improvement
milestones.explanation: Trials would have to define meaningful recovery beforehand and confirm it through repeated assessments of thinking and daily abilities. This would distinguish lasting gains from temporary changes.

milestones.label: Defined safety criteria establish acceptable harms and monitoring
milestones.explanation: Trials would have to assess brain swelling, bleeding and other serious harms against safety limits set beforehand, alongside monitoring needs. This would establish whether benefits justify treatment burdens.

milestones.label: Independent studies confirm lasting benefits across clinical centers
milestones.explanation: Independent studies across clinical centers would have to confirm lasting benefits, individual responses, harms and continued treatment needs. This would establish reproducibility and whom treatment can help.

uncertain: How much lost function can surviving brain systems recover, and how much requires repair or replacement?
What degree and duration of recovery would count as meaningful, and for what proportion of patients?
Could arrest and recovery extend to advanced Alzheimer’s disease or broader patient populations?

page.title: Arrest and reversal of symptomatic Alzheimer’s disease
page.definition: A treatment stops further clinical decline after Alzheimer’s symptoms begin and restores some of the cognition and everyday abilities the person has lost. The initial population has confirmed Alzheimer’s pathology and either mild cognitive impairment or mild dementia. With mild cognitive impairment, a person can still carry out daily tasks independently, even if complex tasks take longer. With mild dementia, some of those tasks require help.

goal.need: About 4.2 million Americans aged 65 or older may have mild cognitive impairment due to Alzheimer’s disease. As impairment progresses, managing medicines or money can require another person’s help. Lecanemab slows decline, but treated patients still worsened on average over 18 months. Sustained recovery could let people resume tasks they had given up and keep doing them independently. Whether people who start treatment in later dementia could regain those abilities is a separate question.

figures.caption: Clarity AD: adjusted mean worsening after 18 months
figures.note: Positive changes indicate worsening. Group averages do not determine individual recovery.

completion.title: A randomized trial establishes sustained arrest and recovery of cognition and daily function.
completion.criterion: In people with confirmed early symptomatic Alzheimer’s disease, a randomized controlled trial demonstrates clinically meaningful gains from pretreatment baseline in both cognition and everyday function, retained without renewed clinical decline through prespecified follow-up, with benefit over control and supporting evidence that the disease course has changed. The registered protocol must justify recovery magnitude and follow-up duration using patient or caregiver anchors. The cited bodies supply no universal numerical recovery cutoff or arrest duration.
completion.set_by: Atlas fallback, informed by FDA and EMA guidance and the NIH clinical-meaningfulness workshop report.
completion.basis: FDA and EMA guidance and the NIH workshop report supply no joint cutoff for the magnitude and duration of cognitive and functional recovery. EMA gives 18 months as an example of a minimum confirmatory trial duration in prodromal or mild-to-moderate disease. The duration for which recovery must persist remains a protocol-specific judgment. A randomized external counterpulsation trial reported gains in cognition and daily function, but enrolled participants by clinical diagnosis without requiring confirmation of Alzheimer’s pathology.

milestones.title: An Alzheimer’s drug has nonclinical pharmacology and toxicology supporting initial human exposure.
milestones.criterion: Pharmacology and toxicology studies in laboratory animals or in vitro provide adequate grounds for the sponsor to conclude that the proposed clinical investigation is reasonably safe. The kind, duration and scope of testing depend on the nature and duration of the proposed human exposure.
milestones.set_by: FDA, 21 CFR 312.23(a)(8), requirements for an investigational new drug application.
milestones.threshold_quote: it is reasonably safe to conduct the proposed clinical investigations.

milestones.title: An Alzheimer’s drug reaches human testing and yields pharmacology and safety data for phase 2.
milestones.criterion: For a U.S. investigation subject to an investigational new drug application, human dosing begins after the application takes effect. Phase 1 studies characterize human pharmacology and adverse effects with increasing doses and provide enough information on pharmacokinetics and pharmacological effects to design a well-controlled phase 2 study.
milestones.set_by: FDA, 21 CFR 312.20(b) and 312.21(a), authorization and phase 1 objectives.
milestones.threshold_quote: to permit the design of well-controlled, scientifically valid, Phase 2 studies.

milestones.title: A controlled phase 2 study finds preliminary efficacy in symptomatic Alzheimer’s disease.
milestones.criterion: A controlled phase 2 study in patients with symptomatic Alzheimer’s disease provides preliminary evidence of effectiveness for the intended indication and characterizes common short-term adverse effects and risks.
milestones.set_by: FDA, 21 CFR 312.21(b)–(c), phase 2 objectives and the preliminary evidence preceding phase 3.
milestones.threshold_quote: after preliminary evidence suggesting effectiveness of the drug has been obtained

milestones.title: A confirmatory trial shows benefit in both cognition and daily function in Stage 3 Alzheimer’s disease.
milestones.criterion: For patients with Stage 3 Alzheimer’s disease approaching overt dementia, a confirmatory trial demonstrates favorable effects on both cognition and daily functioning. The trial may assess the domains separately or use one integrated scale that adequately and meaningfully assesses the effect on each domain.
milestones.set_by: FDA, March 2024 revised draft guidance, section IV.D.3, Stage 3 Alzheimer’s disease; nonbinding and not final.
milestones.threshold_quote: favorably affects the observed impairments in both cognition and daily functioning.

milestones.title: A responder improves in cognition without worsening in either daily function or global clinical status.
milestones.criterion: Prespecify a clinically relevant degree of cognitive improvement from baseline, taking account of the expected course of disease over the trial. Report the proportion of patients who reach that improvement and whose daily function and global clinical status both remain stable or improve.
milestones.set_by: EMA CHMP, 2018 guideline, section 8.3.1; an illustrative symptomatic-treatment responder definition, without a universal numerical cutoff.
milestones.threshold_quote: improved to a relevant pre-specified degree in the cognitive endpoint and at least not worsened in the two other domains (function and global).

milestones.title: A randomized trial demonstrates recovery of both cognition and everyday function from baseline.
milestones.criterion: At a prespecified endpoint in a randomized trial, a disease-modifying treatment produces clinically meaningful gains from pretreatment baseline in both cognition and everyday function, with superiority to control. The protocol prospectively justifies the magnitude of recovery using patient or caregiver assessments as anchors.
milestones.set_by: Atlas fallback: FDA and EMA guidance and the NIH workshop report do not specify a combined cognitive-and-functional recovery threshold.

milestones.title: A biologic drug engages its target and shows preliminary efficacy in an Alzheimer’s animal model.
milestones.criterion: In a relevant animal model, the candidate shows efficacy on a clinically relevant biochemical, pathological, behavioral or functional measure. It also shows target engagement at the intended site of action through a measure of binding or a proximal downstream effect.
milestones.set_by: National Institute on Aging, Alzheimer’s Drug-Development Program, PAR-25-297, early-stage entry criteria for biologics
milestones.threshold_quote: Established preliminary in-vivo efficacy and target engagement data using agent(s) in relevant animal model(s).

not_found: No joint numerical recovery threshold, minimum arrest duration or required responder fraction was found in the FDA, EMA, NIH and Alzheimer’s Association documents examined.
Animal group sizes are not provided in TGA’s published summary of lecanemab’s nonclinical studies.
No FDA, EMA or Alzheimer’s Association statement was found that judges sustained clinical recovery unattainable or unworthy of pursuit.

results.finding: In a first-in-human BAN2401 study of 80 people with mild-to-moderate Alzheimer’s disease, the serum terminal half-life was about 7 days.
results.quote: BAN2401 exposure was approximately dose proportional, with a serum terminal elimination half-life of ~7 days.

results.finding: Phase 2 donanemab (n=257 across monotherapy and placebo) favored placebo-adjusted iADRS change by 3.2 points.
results.detail: The sample size excludes the discontinued 15-person donanemab plus BACE inhibitor arm. The FDA report presents broader adverse-event rates for phase 3 AACI.
results.quote:
The Phase 2 Study AACG 
provided confirmatory evidence of effectiveness with the primary endpoint of iADRS (3.2; 95% 
CI 0.1, 6.3; p-value = 0.04).

results.finding: Phase 3 donanemab (n=1,736 randomized) reduced decline versus placebo by 1.7 points on instrumental activities of daily living.
results.detail: The reported domain results cover the overall and intermediate-tau populations. Baseline global CDR scores in the overall population included 0.5, 1, and 2.
results.quote:
At Week 76, the donanemab arm compared to the placebo arm had statistically significantly less 
decline as measured by ADCS-iADL.

results.finding: Phase 3 donanemab (n=1,599 in the iADRS analysis) showed a 10.2-point adjusted mean iADRS decline from baseline.
results.detail: The prespecified efficacy objective was slowing progression. The exact treatment-arm decline appears in Table 4.

results.finding: Donepezil in mice and rats (sample sizes unreported) had a single-dose oral median lethal dose of 32 mg/kg in rats.
results.detail: The label compares animal toxicity with the marketed human dose. It gives no initial clinical dose or exposure duration.
results.quote: The estimated median lethal dose of donepezil hydrochloride following administration of a single oral dose in mice and rats is 45 and 32 mg/kg, respectively, or approximately 225 and 160 times the maximum recommended human dose of 10 mg per day.

results.finding: Donepezil 10 mg daily inhibited erythrocyte acetylcholinesterase by 77.3% at steady state in Alzheimer’s dementia trial participants (sample size unreported).
results.quote: In patients with Alzheimer's Dementia participating in clinical trials, administration of single daily doses of 5 mg or 10 mg of donepezil produced steady-state inhibition of acetylcholinesterase activity (measured in erythrocyte membranes) of 63.6% and 77.3%, respectively when measured post dose.

results.finding: In a six-month Alzheimer’s dementia trial (n=365 intent-to-treat), 21% of patients assigned to donepezil 10 mg met the composite responder definition.
In the six-month Alzheimer’s dementia trial (n=365 intent-to-treat), 21% on donepezil 10 mg improved cognitively with stable or improved daily function and global status.
In a 46-participant phase 1b trial in mild Alzheimer’s disease, 94% of MAPTRx recipients reported adverse events.
results.detail: The authors identified further extension data as important for refining the dose and dosing interval.
results.quote:
Adverse events 
were reported in 94% of MAPTRx-treated patients and 75% of placebo-treated 
patients; all were mild or moderate.

results.finding: Intensive lifestyle intervention in symptomatic Alzheimer’s disease (n = 49 analyzed) favored usual care on CGIC at p = 0.001.
results.detail: The two withdrawals document difficulty continuing the program. The paper gives no adverse-event frequencies.
results.quote:
These scores improved in the intervention group and worsened in the control group.
(Fisher’s exact
p
-value = 0.001).

results.finding: Intensive lifestyle intervention in early symptomatic Alzheimer’s disease (n = 49 analyzed) favored control by 0.44 CDR-SB points.
results.quote:
These scores worsened significantly more in the control group (from 3.34 to 3.86) than in the intervention group (from 3.27 to 3.35), mean group difference = 0.44,
p
= 0.032 (Table
3
and Fig.
4
).

results.finding: Among 24 lifestyle intervention participants with early symptomatic Alzheimer’s disease, 10 improved on CGIC.
results.quote: Of the 24 patients in the intervention group, 10 showed improvement as measured by the CGIC test, 7 were unchanged, and 7 worsened.

results.finding: In early symptomatic Alzheimer’s disease (n = 48 with valid ADAS-Cog testing), lifestyle intervention favored control by 1.923 ADAS-Cog points.
results.detail: Plasma Aβ42/40 moved in a favorable direction. The study did not directly assess changes in brain pathology.
results.quote:
These scores improved in the intervention group (from 21.551 to 20.536) and worsened in the randomized control group (from 21.252 to 22.160), mean group difference of change = 1.923 points,
p
= 0.053 (Table
3
and Fig.
3
).

results.finding: FDA found lecanemab’s nonclinical package sufficient for a licensing submission covering patients aged ≥50 years. Nonclinical sample sizes were unreported.
results.detail: Page 47 records FDA’s conclusion for the licensing submission. The 2021 minutes also request comparability data for the pivotal nonclinical material and the commercial product.
results.quote:
Based on the information provided in the briefing document, the completed nonclinical 
studies remain sufficient to support submission of a BLA for the use of BAN2401 in patients 
≥ 50 years of age.

results.finding: Lecanemab entered ascending-dose testing in patients with Alzheimer’s disease under an IND active since July 29, 2010. Sample size unreported.
results.detail: Page 38 records the IND date and trial sequence. Page 9 lists safety, tolerability, pharmacodynamic response, and pharmacokinetics as study objectives.
results.quote:
Study 201 was begun after the initial IND study, Study BAN2401-G000-101 (Study 101), was 
conducted. Study 101 was a single and multiple ascending dose study conducted in patients with 
mild to moderate Alzheimer’s disease.

results.finding: In lecanemab Study 201 (n=856), the top-dose arm had a 64% probability of reaching the prespecified target for slowing ADCOMS decline.
results.detail: Page 32 reports the primary analysis. The month-18 CDR-SB signal reflected less decline versus placebo. The pooled high-dose repeated-measures estimate had a confidence interval spanning zero.
results.quote:
At 12 months, the 10 mg/kg biweekly arm had 64% 
probability to be better than placebo by 25% , which missed the 80% threshold for the primary outcome.

results.finding: In Clarity AD (n=1,795 randomized), lecanemab limited daily function decline by 2.0 points versus placebo.
results.detail: The modified intention-to-treat population included 1,734 participants, about 62% with mild cognitive impairment and 38% with mild dementia.
results.quote:
The adjusted mean change from baseline at 18 
months in the ADCS-MCI-ADL score was −3.5 in 
the lecanemab group and −5.5 in the placebo 
group (difference, 2.0; 95% CI, 1.2 to 2.8; P<0.001) 
(Fig. 2E and Table 2).

results.finding: In Clarity AD (n=1,795 randomized), cognition worsened by 4.14 ADAS-cog14 points from baseline with lecanemab at 18 months.
results.detail: The prospective CDR-SB target concerned less decline relative to placebo. The paper gives no anchor-based justification for a magnitude of recovery from baseline.
results.quote:
The adjusted 
mean change from baseline at 18 months in the 
ADAS-cog14 score was 4.14 in the lecanemab 
group and 5.58 in the placebo group

results.finding: In APP NL-G-F knock-in mice, mB28 reduced brain Aβ oligomers by ~93% versus isotype control (28 treated, 29 controls).
results.detail: The study used mB28, the murinized version of B28, at 15 mg/kg intraperitoneally each week starting at 4 months of age, after plaque deposition had begun.
results.quote: mB28 treatment reduced oAβ by a striking ~93% compared to the mIgG placebo

results.finding: Lecanemab received an FDA Study May Proceed Letter on October 27, 2010. Sample size for this regulatory finding is not applicable.
results.quote:
A Study May Proceed Letter was issued to the applicant on 
October 27, 2010.

results.finding: In a phase 1 donanemab study (N=63), mild to moderate infusion reactions occurred in 6 of 37 patients with Alzheimer’s disease who received IV donanemab.
results.detail: The authors could not model the dose–exposure–effect relationship because treatment-emergent antidrug antibodies may have affected pharmacokinetics.
results.quote: The most common adverse event was mild to moderate infusion reactions and was experienced by 6 of 37 patients with AD who had IV dosing.

results.finding: In the Clarity AD low-tau subgroup (n=141 at baseline), lecanemab’s cognitive improvement rate exceeded placebo’s by 36 percentage points at 18 months.
results.detail: The numerical improvement rates are from Figure 2. The baseline subgroup count is larger than the number assessed at 18 months. The low-tau mean cognitive change favored lecanemab with p=0.20, and the poster describes the mean changes on both scales as reduced decline.

definition = "A treatment stops further clinical decline after Alzheimer\u2019s symptoms begin and restores some of the cognition and everyday abilities the person has lost. The initial population has confirmed Alzheimer\u2019s pathology and either mild cognitive impairment or mild dementia. With mild cognitive impairment, a person can still carry out daily tasks independently, even if complex tasks take longer. With mild dementia, some of those tasks require help.". Reason: The distinction between mild cognitive impairment and mild dementia turns on independence in daily activities, which the current definition leaves unclear.

goal.need = "About 4.2 million Americans aged 65 or older may have mild cognitive impairment due to Alzheimer\u2019s disease. As impairment progresses, managing medicines or money can require another person\u2019s help. Lecanemab slows decline, but treated patients still worsened on average over 18 months. Sustained recovery could let people resume tasks they had given up and keep doing them independently. Whether people who start treatment in later dementia could regain those abilities is a separate question.". Reason: The current rationale explains a rating scale and an adverse event but gives neither the size of the early symptomatic population nor the everyday consequence of recovery.

add statement by U.S. Congress, National Alzheimer’s Project Act, 2011: "accelerate the development of treatments that would prevent, halt, or reverse the course of Alzheimer’s". Reason: The founding statute explicitly names reversal of the disease course as a national goal and predates the departmental statements.

add not found: "No FDA, EMA or Alzheimer’s Association statement was found that judges sustained clinical recovery unattainable or unworthy of pursuit.". Reason: The absence of an established treatment and an institutional judgment that recovery is unattainable are distinct claims.

edit completion: basis = "FDA and EMA guidance and the NIH workshop report supply no joint cutoff for the magnitude and duration of cognitive and functional recovery. EMA gives 18 months as an example of a minimum confirmatory trial duration in prodromal or mild-to-moderate disease. The duration for which recovery must persist remains a protocol-specific judgment. A randomized external counterpulsation trial reported gains in cognition and daily function, but enrolled participants by clinical diagnosis without requiring confirmation of Alzheimer\u2019s pathology."; refs = [5, 6, 7, 3, 8, 23]. Reason: The basis omits EMA’s trial-duration example and a randomized clinical improvement result whose population lacked confirmation of Alzheimer’s pathology.

add milestone after None: "A biologic drug engages its target and shows preliminary efficacy in an Alzheimer’s animal model.". Reason: The first existing milestone tests safety for human exposure and leaves out laboratory evidence that a candidate engages its target and has an effect in a disease model.

edit m1: criterion = "Pharmacology and toxicology studies in laboratory animals or in vitro provide adequate grounds for the sponsor to conclude that the proposed clinical investigation is reasonably safe. The kind, duration and scope of testing depend on the nature and duration of the proposed human exposure."; threshold_quote = "it is reasonably safe to conduct the proposed clinical investigations."; threshold_ref = 9. Reason: The lecanemab dossier findings obscure the regulatory judgment that determines readiness for the proposed human exposure.

edit m2: criterion = "For a U.S. investigation subject to an investigational new drug application, human dosing begins after the application takes effect. Phase 1 studies characterize human pharmacology and adverse effects with increasing doses and provide enough information on pharmacokinetics and pharmacological effects to design a well-controlled phase 2 study."; threshold_quote = "to permit the design of well-controlled, scientifically valid, Phase 2 studies."; threshold_ref = 11. Reason: The phase 1 criterion mixes one drug’s doses and sample size with the information needed to design phase 2.

edit m3: criterion = "A controlled phase 2 study in patients with symptomatic Alzheimer\u2019s disease provides preliminary evidence of effectiveness for the intended indication and characterizes common short-term adverse effects and risks."; threshold_quote = "after preliminary evidence suggesting effectiveness of the drug has been obtained"; threshold_ref = 11. Reason: Study 201’s probability target belongs to that trial and obscures the general phase 2 test.

edit m4: title = "A confirmatory trial shows benefit in both cognition and daily function in Stage 3 Alzheimer\u2019s disease."; criterion = "For patients with Stage 3 Alzheimer\u2019s disease approaching overt dementia, a confirmatory trial demonstrates favorable effects on both cognition and daily functioning. The trial may assess the domains separately or use one integrated scale that adequately and meaningfully assesses the effect on each domain."; threshold_quote = "favorably affects the observed impairments in both cognition and daily functioning."; threshold_ref = 5. Reason: The trial and extension results obscure the FDA draft’s condition for using an integrated clinical scale at Stage 3.

edit m5: title = "A responder improves in cognition without worsening in either daily function or global clinical status."; criterion = "Prespecify a clinically relevant degree of cognitive improvement from baseline, taking account of the expected course of disease over the trial. Report the proportion of patients who reach that improvement and whose daily function and global clinical status both remain stable or improve."; threshold_quote = "improved to a relevant pre-specified degree in the cognitive endpoint and at least not worsened in the two other domains (function and global)."; threshold_ref = 6. Reason: The current wording blurs an individual responder definition with group averages and a donepezil-specific four-point cutoff.

edit m6: criterion = "At a prespecified endpoint in a randomized trial, a disease-modifying treatment produces clinically meaningful gains from pretreatment baseline in both cognition and everyday function, with superiority to control. The protocol prospectively justifies the magnitude of recovery using patient or caregiver assessments as anchors.". Reason: The endpoint test currently includes a verdict on particular anti-amyloid studies and repeats the follow-up test for completion.
